_meta.review_gate: This file must get a physician review pass before it is shown to a learner. Do not ship without it.
_meta.rules: No dosing. No titration. No 'how to take it'. No overdose or toxicity information. Educational one-liners only.

medications.how_it_works: Helps keep more serotonin available between brain cells, which can steady mood over several weeks.
medications.good_to_know: Usually takes 4–6 weeks to show its full effect.

medications.how_it_works: Keeps more serotonin available between brain cells.
medications.good_to_know: Stays in the body longer than most others in its family.

medications.how_it_works: Keeps more serotonin available between brain cells.
medications.good_to_know: Often chosen when someone is dealing with both low mood and worry.

medications.how_it_works: Keeps more serotonin available between brain cells.
medications.good_to_know: A close relative of escitalopram.

medications.how_it_works: Keeps more serotonin available between brain cells.
medications.good_to_know: Needs to be stopped slowly rather than all at once.

medications.how_it_works: Keeps more serotonin available between brain cells.
medications.good_to_know: Used most often for OCD.

medications.how_it_works: Keeps more of two messengers available — serotonin and norepinephrine.
medications.good_to_know: Needs to be stopped slowly rather than all at once.

medications.how_it_works: Keeps more serotonin and norepinephrine available.
medications.good_to_know: Also used for some kinds of long-lasting physical pain.

medications.how_it_works: Keeps more serotonin and norepinephrine available.
medications.good_to_know: A close relative of venlafaxine.

medications.how_it_works: Works on dopamine and norepinephrine rather than serotonin.
medications.good_to_know: Tends to be energizing rather than sedating.

medications.how_it_works: Nudges serotonin and norepinephrine signalling in a different way from the SSRIs.
medications.good_to_know: Often makes people sleepy, so it is usually taken at night.

medications.how_it_works: Affects serotonin signalling and is strongly sedating.
medications.good_to_know: Used far more often for sleep than for mood.

medications.how_it_works: Acts on several different serotonin receptors at once.
medications.good_to_know: Sometimes chosen when concentration is a big part of the problem.

medications.how_it_works: Combines an SSRI-like effect with an extra action on one serotonin receptor.
medications.good_to_know: Usually taken with food.

medications.how_it_works: An older medicine that raises serotonin and norepinephrine, plus several other effects.
medications.good_to_know: One of the first antidepressants ever made; still used today, often for other reasons.

medications.how_it_works: Raises norepinephrine more than serotonin.
medications.good_to_know: Generally easier to tolerate than older members of its family.

medications.how_it_works: The most serotonin-focused of the older antidepressants.
medications.good_to_know: Was the first medicine shown to help OCD.

medications.how_it_works: Raises serotonin and norepinephrine.
medications.good_to_know: Historically important — it helped show that panic attacks respond to medicine.

medications.how_it_works: Blocks an enzyme that breaks down several brain messengers, so more of them stay around.
medications.good_to_know: Comes with a list of foods and other medicines to avoid, so it is used carefully.

medications.how_it_works: Blocks the enzyme that breaks down several brain messengers.
medications.good_to_know: Usually kept for depression that has not responded to other options.

medications.how_it_works: Same idea as other MAOIs, but delivered through a skin patch.
medications.good_to_know: The patch form skips the stomach, which changes what needs to be avoided.

medications.how_it_works: Boosts GABA, the brain's main calming signal, which quiets things down quickly.
medications.good_to_know: Works within minutes, which is why it is generally used short-term.

medications.how_it_works: Boosts the brain's calming GABA signal.
medications.good_to_know: Fast-acting and short-lasting.

medications.how_it_works: Boosts the brain's calming GABA signal.
medications.good_to_know: Lasts longer in the body than most of its relatives.

medications.how_it_works: Boosts the brain's calming GABA signal.
medications.good_to_know: One of the oldest medicines in this family.

medications.how_it_works: Acts on a particular serotonin receptor rather than on GABA.
medications.good_to_know: Builds up slowly over weeks instead of working right away.

medications.how_it_works: Blocks histamine, which has a calming and sleepy side effect.
medications.good_to_know: Related to allergy medicines.

medications.how_it_works: Blocks adrenaline's effect on the body, so the heart pounding and shaky hands settle.
medications.good_to_know: Works on the physical part of fear, not on the worrying thoughts.

medications.how_it_works: A simple mineral salt that steadies mood swings; exactly how it does this is still being studied.
medications.good_to_know: Needs regular blood tests while someone is taking it.

medications.how_it_works: Calms overactive electrical signalling in the brain.
medications.good_to_know: Started very slowly, because of a rash that needs to be watched for.

medications.how_it_works: Raises GABA activity and steadies electrical signalling.
medications.good_to_know: Originally developed as a seizure medicine.

medications.how_it_works: Steadies electrical signalling in nerve cells.
medications.good_to_know: Interacts with a lot of other medicines.

medications.how_it_works: Steadies dopamine signalling — turning it down where it is too high and up where it is too low.
medications.good_to_know: Sometimes added to an antidepressant when that alone is not enough.

medications.how_it_works: Blocks certain dopamine and serotonin receptors.
medications.good_to_know: Often quite sedating.

medications.how_it_works: Blocks certain dopamine and serotonin receptors.
medications.good_to_know: One of the most widely used medicines in its family.

medications.how_it_works: Blocks several dopamine and serotonin receptors.
medications.good_to_know: Effective, but weight and blood sugar need watching.

medications.how_it_works: Blocks certain dopamine and serotonin receptors.
medications.good_to_know: Taken with food so the body can absorb it properly.

medications.how_it_works: Blocks certain dopamine and serotonin receptors.
medications.good_to_know: Less likely than some relatives to cause weight gain.

medications.how_it_works: Increases dopamine and norepinephrine in the parts of the brain that handle focus.
medications.good_to_know: Works the same day rather than over weeks.

medications.how_it_works: A refined version of methylphenidate that raises dopamine and norepinephrine.
medications.good_to_know: Closely related to Ritalin.

medications.how_it_works: Increases dopamine and norepinephrine activity, improving focus and follow-through.
medications.good_to_know: Comes in short-acting and long-acting versions.

medications.how_it_works: Inactive until the body converts it, then raises dopamine and norepinephrine.
medications.good_to_know: The slow conversion gives it a smoother, longer effect.

medications.how_it_works: Raises norepinephrine only — no stimulant effect.
medications.good_to_know: Takes several weeks to work, unlike the stimulants.

medications.how_it_works: Acts on norepinephrine receptors in the front of the brain, which helps with impulse control.
medications.good_to_know: Can be calming, so it is sometimes taken in the evening.

medications.how_it_works: Turns down norepinephrine signalling.
medications.good_to_know: Was originally a blood pressure medicine.

medications.how_it_works: Raises norepinephrine without a stimulant effect.
medications.good_to_know: One of the newer options for ADHD.

medications.how_it_works: Copies the hormone the brain releases at dusk to signal that it is night.
medications.good_to_know: Helps most with the timing of sleep rather than the depth of it.

medications.how_it_works: Acts on the brain's melatonin receptors more strongly than melatonin itself.
medications.good_to_know: Aimed at trouble falling asleep rather than staying asleep.

medications.how_it_works: Boosts the brain's calming GABA signal in a way tuned toward sleep.
medications.good_to_know: Meant for short stretches, not indefinitely.

medications.how_it_works: Boosts the brain's calming GABA signal.
medications.good_to_know: Lasts a bit longer through the night than zolpidem.

medications.how_it_works: At a very small amount it blocks histamine, which helps people stay asleep.
medications.good_to_know: The same molecule works as an antidepressant at much larger amounts.

medications.how_it_works: Blocks orexin, the signal that keeps the brain awake, instead of forcing sleep.
medications.good_to_know: A newer approach — it turns down wakefulness rather than turning up sleepiness.
